cards.front: Recall a key point about Subjunctive Mood & Advanced Syntax
cards.back: The subjunctive mood expresses possibility, purpose, wish, or subordinate action — unlike the indicative, which states facts.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Subjunctive Mood & Advanced Syntax
cards.back: Present subjunctive is formed by changing the stem vowel: 1st conjugation changes -a- to -e- (muset), 2nd changes -e- to -ea- (moneas), 3rd/4th change to -a- (ducamus, audiamus).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Subjunctive Mood & Advanced Syntax
cards.back: Imperfect subjunctive is formed by adding -re to the infinitive: laudarem (I would praise / I might praise).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Subjunctive Mood & Advanced Syntax
cards.back: Purpose clauses: ut + subjunctive = 'in order to' (positive); ne + subjunctive = 'in order not to' (negative). Example: venit ut pater videret (he came in order that his father might see).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Subjunctive Mood & Advanced Syntax
cards.back: Result clauses: ut + subjunctive after tam/ita/tantus/talis = 'so...that'. Example: tam fortis erat ut hostes vinceret (he was so brave that he conquered the enemy).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Subjunctive Mood & Advanced Syntax
cards.back: Indirect commands: after verbs of ordering/asking/persuading + ut/ne + subjunctive. Example: rex imperavit ut milites venirent (the king ordered that the soldiers should come).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Subjunctive Mood & Advanced Syntax
cards.back: Cum clauses: cum + subjunctive can mean 'when' (temporal), 'since' (causal), or 'although' (concessive). Context determines the meaning.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Subjunctive Mood & Advanced Syntax
cards.back: Indirect questions use the subjunctive: rogat ubi puer sit (he asks where the boy is). The verb of the subordinate question is subjunctive.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Subjunctive Mood & Advanced Syntax
cards.back: Conditional sentences: si + subjunctive in the protasis (if clause), with the apodosis (main clause) also in the subjunctive for unreal conditions.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Subjunctive Mood & Advanced Syntax
cards.back: The gerundive (future passive participle) expresses obligation: gerundive of obligation — mihi parendum est (I must be obeyed / I must obey).

cards.front: What should you know about gcse latin exam tips — subjunctive mood & advanced syntax?
cards.back: 1. For Subjunctive Mood & Advanced Syntax, use a range of vocabulary and complex grammatical structures to access higher marks 2. When writing about Subjunctive Mood & Advanced Syntax, include opinions and justifications, not just descriptions 5. For listening and reading, focus on key words and cognates to extract meaning
